history.summary: IDENTITY FLAG: the best-supported referent for this row is the Maa Ramachandi cave temple on the bank of the Ib river at Rampur near Brajrajnagar, Jharsuguda district - a riverside rock-cave shrine that is submerged during the monsoon and is documented in multiple video vlogs and listed by Airports Authority of India as a Jharsuguda tourist place. Local legend links it to Lord Rama's exile (vanvas) and says Veer Surendra Sai took refuge here; one vlog calls it an 8th-century Kalinga temple and names Ramnavami as its main festival - all of this is video/local-legend sourcing only and needs verification. CSV town 'Jharsuguda' is imprecise: the shrine is near Brajrajnagar/Rampur, ~30 km from Jharsuguda city. AMBIGUITY NOTE: a separate 'Ramachandi Temple' place listing exists at Adhapara, Banaharapali (21.708979, 83.847189); if the CSV intends that shrine instead, this file's identity must change. Coordinates here are approximate for the Rampur/Ib river bank cave temple - verify exactly.

name: Maa Ramachandi Temple
town_description: Brajrajnagar is an industrial town in Jharsuguda district of western Odisha on the Ib river, once a major coal-mining centre. The Ramachandi cave shrine lies at Rampur near Brajrajnagar on the Ib river bank and is partly submerged in the monsoon. Coordinates (21.88, 83.9) are approximate for the Rampur cave temple - verify exactly before use; a separate Ramachandi Temple listing exists at Banaharapali.
